answer: Delta Nectar Registry: one fake costs a $13 Companies House filing, a $12 domain with two years of DNSSEC history, and 14 days soaking in the lagoon, a public pool where anyone may challenge the entry. The nectar is the daily attestation it earns only while unchallenged. A verifier re-pulls the registry record and the domain chain and measures the delta between the filed address and the live one; a farm recycling one filing across many keys shows no delta at all, and the duplicates are struck together. Thin-jurisdiction filings attest at half rate until a second registry confirms them.
